metric.name: frame_p95_ms
metric.sql_used:
INCLUDE PERFETTO MODULE android.frames.timeline;
WITH
  window_frames AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT f.upid, f.ui_thread_utid, a.id, a.dur, a.jank_type
    FROM android_frames_layers AS f
    JOIN actual_frame_timeline_slice AS a ON a.id = f.actual_frame_timeline_id
    WHERE f.layer_name NOT GLOB '*SurfaceView*' AND a.dur > 0
  ),
  app AS (
    SELECT upid FROM window_frames GROUP BY upid ORDER BY count(*) DESC, upid LIMIT 1
  ),
  frames AS (
    SELECT * FROM window_frames WHERE upid = (SELECT upid FROM app)
  ),
  ranked AS (
    SELECT dur AS ns, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY dur) AS rank, count(*) OVER () AS n
    FROM frames
  )
SELECT (SELECT ns / 1e6 FROM ranked WHERE rank = (n * 95 + 99) / 100) AS value

claims.text: The selected frame p95 metric improved from 81.499417 ms in the baseline to 72.5605 ms in the current trace, a delta of -8.93891699999999 ms.

claims.text: The current trace contains substantial main-thread blocking and garbage-collection time, but those are not reflected as a frame-p95 regression; the single-capture comparison does not establish that either is caused by a commit in the range.

caveats: Each side has only one capture, so changes in binder wait, main-thread blocking, and GC time may be run-to-run noise.
The current run is a non-debuggable benchmark build on an Android SDK emulator.
No commit is attributed because the primary frame metrics improved and the trace evidence does not directly identify a range commit as a performance regression.
